one_line: Cold-chain temperature monitoring for small food businesses splits into no-fee Wi-Fi sensors ($149-$199 once), small metered subscriptions ($0-$45 per month, or $5-$21 per sensor per month mid-market), installed per-location offers ($77-$210 per location per month, plus roughly $50-$70 per sensor of onboarding where charged), zone-based compliance plans ($45-$65 per zone per month plus a $2,500 per-site gateway and $495 per zone upfront), and quote-only enterprise programs, with one-time configuration priced separately ($115 per Kitchen Brains subscription, $495 per ChirpDat zone) and a New Jersey contractor quoting a typical installed job at $1,200-$8,000.

what_is_included_vs_extra.point: At the low end the hardware is the product: Temp Stick is $149 once on sale ($159 regular), and the product page says the unlimited logging and 24/7 monitoring are free for the lifetime of the sensor, so the buyer pays no recurring fee but gets no calibration certificates, no audit-ready HACCP report pack and no escalation service.

Per-sensor subscriptions diverge on what the monthly fee covers: Sensor Easy bundles app, alerts and inspection reporting for $5/month up to five sensors, while Standard Merchant Services charges $10-$15 per sensor per month but adds a $49.99-$69.99 per-sensor onboarding/installation fee on top.

Installed hardware is frequently the biggest single line: Kitchen Brains charges $529 per gateway and $184 per sensor before the $10/month per-sensor subscription and a $115 one-time configuration fee.

TemperatureWise separates one-time hardware from an annual per-sensor fee: $200 per LoRa sensor (or $25 per Bluetooth sensor), a $100/$250/$450 gateway per site, then $250 per sensor per year, with dashboard, alerts and setup explicitly at no extra charge and cellular the only other recurring cost ($125 once plus $50 a year).

ChirpDat shows what a compliance-grade tier adds over basic alerting: the $65/zone Compliance plan includes an annual NIST-traceable sensor swap, a human escalation call tree and audit-prep reports, versus $45/zone for alerts, dashboards and history only.

ChirpDat's zone price covers the sensors for that zone (up to three per equipment zone) but not the gateway, commissioning, licensed electrical work, specialized instrumentation or white-glove onsite installation, all of which are quoted separately.

ThermoWorks bundles users and devices into the subscription but meters devices hard: plan caps run 10/16/24/48/100 devices, with overage at $0.90, $0.83 and $0.79 per additional device depending on tier.

Monnit separates the software license from the hardware: the annual license is cheap (from $45/year for up to 6 sensors) but sensors, gateway and installation are bought separately, and the free Basic tier lacks Premiere's multi-user and faster check-in features.
ConnectedFresh puts hardware inside the annual subscription (sensors pre-configured, replaced if they fail), and models about $150 per monitored unit only for buyers who purchase hardware outright.

SmartSense sells an all-inclusive asset-based subscription and publishes an included-items list rather than prices: unlimited users, equipment per asset, cellular networking and data, no-cost replacement of failed or obsolete devices for the term, NIST-certified recalibration, API access, onboarding and a dedicated success manager.

ComplianceMate's annual subscription includes ongoing 24/7 support and real-time alerting with live call-center escalation, but the equipment and the customized checklist configuration are separate one-time fees.

Per-location pricing that includes unlimited users is now a selling point: Sensitii states it prices per location and never per seat, that every plan includes unlimited users, that the gateway and sensors are in the subscription with no upfront hardware, and that annual billing gets one month free. Its page publishes no dollar figures, so no Sensitii price is given here.

buyer_complaints.complaint: The SmartSense iOS app carries a 2.6 out of 5 rating from 28 ratings, a weak signal for a platform sold as enterprise-grade; review text was not readable on the listing.

Jolt buyers report contract lock-in: reviewers describe having to keep paying through the year after a feature did not work for them, and the platform is repeatedly described as expensive with no trial.

ComplianceMate's own troubleshooting guidance flags sensors damaged by moisture or corrosion, placement/obstruction problems and gaps in readings, which are the practical failure modes buyers complain about with wireless probes.

Cheap Wi-Fi sensors are the segment's reliability weak point: operator and user reports describe dropped Wi-Fi connections, re-pairing, and devices that fail to reconnect after router downtime, with alerts silently lost.

Temp Stick monitors ambient air only, cannot be recalibrated (only offset in settings), and is not a substitute for a calibrated food probe - a common source of misunderstanding for buyers expecting one device to cover all HACCP checks.

Testo shut down the free Saveris Cloud tier and moved existing users to a paid subscription; the complaint is documented on an advocacy wiki rather than by Testo, so treat it as a one-sided account of a pricing change.

price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: $0-$45 per month of software, or $149-$250 one-time hardware, equivalent to roughly $5-$21 per sensor per month
price_ranges.mid_market: $77-$210 per location per month (about $10-$21 per monitored unit plus a $29-$150 platform fee), plus roughly $50-$70 per sensor of onboarding/installation where charged, and separate one-time configuration fees on top (Kitchen Brains $115 configuration; ChirpDat $495 per zone)
price_ranges.full_service_or_custom: $1,200-$8,000 upfront plus $1,200-$3,000 per store per year, or $45-$65 per zone per month with a $2,500 per-site gateway and $495 per zone upfront; enterprise vendors quote only
price_ranges.inference_note: Every endpoint traces to a published number and is my arithmetic, not a survey average. Low: $0 (ThermoWorks Free), $3/$9/$35/month (ThermoWorks Home/Pro/Business Pro), $45.00/year (Monnit Premiere 6-sensor license), $29 hub + $8/sensor (Zip); hardware $149 (Temp Stick sale price), $200 sensor and $250 gateway (TemperatureWise), $219.70 kit (Sensor Easy); per-sensor month equivalent from $5 (Sensor Easy) through $8 (Zip), $10 (Kitchen Brains), $10-$15 (Standard Merchant Services) to about $21 (TemperatureWise's $250/sensor/year). Mid: $77 is Zip at six sensors ($29 + 6 x $8); $210 is ConnectedFresh's own stated $190-$210 for a 4-6 unit restaurant; the per-unit band runs $10 (ConnectedFresh, Standard Merchant Services 12-month) to about $21 (TemperatureWise); the $29-$150 platform fee spans Zip's hub and ConnectedFresh's per-location fee; onboarding is $69.99/$59.99/$49.99 per sensor (Standard Merchant Services) and configuration fees are $115 (Kitchen Brains, per subscription) and $495 per zone (ChirpDat). Full-service: the $1,200-$8,000 upfront and $1,200-$3,000/year figures are a New Jersey contractor's stated typical project range and a third-party (not vendor) ComplianceMate estimate; the $45-$65 per zone plus $2,500 gateway plus $495 per zone is ChirpDat's published list. The ranges overlap deliberately because vendors sell different units (sensor, zone, location, device).

implications_for_consultancy: Inference: the defensible position is the 'installed and looked after' tier at roughly $99-$189 per location per month for 4-8 monitored units with hardware included. Reasoning: that is at or below ConnectedFresh's own stated $190-$210/month for a 4-6 unit restaurant and clearly below what its published formula ($150 per location + about $10 per monitored unit) would produce at 8 units - about $230/month, which is my arithmetic from their rates, not a quoted price - while staying above the $29 hub + $8/sensor self-install price where the buyer does the work and gets no HACCP paperwork.

Inference: charge a one-time setup in the $500-$1,500 band for a single site. Buyers already accept $49.99-$69.99 per sensor of onboarding (Standard Merchant Services), a $115 configuration fee (Kitchen Brains), a $2,500 gateway plus $495 per zone (ChirpDat), and a $1,200-$8,000 typical installed range from an NJ refrigeration firm - so a 4-8 unit install at $500-$1,500 reads as normal rather than premium.

Inference: keep the recurring fee per monitored unit at $10-$21 and never per user. Competitors that price per location bundle users - ThermoWorks Business Pro/Business Pro Plus list unlimited users, Standard Merchant Services' 12-month plan lists unlimited users, Sensitii says it prices per location and never per seat, and SmartSense by Digi lists unlimited users among what its subscription includes - so per-seat pricing would look out of step and penalise putting alerts in front of the closing manager.

Inference: the price step from $45 to $65 per zone (ChirpDat Monitor to Compliance) is the market's own valuation of HACCP logs, an annual NIST-traceable sensor swap, an escalation call tree and audit reports - roughly a 44% uplift. A local consultancy can justify a similar uplift by bundling calibration/replacement, written HACCP procedures, inspection-day support and after-hours escalation, all of which self-serve kits do not include.

Inference: a pilot at $250-$500 for 30-60 days is defensible because free or low-cost entry already exists at the low end (ThermoWorks free tier, Monnit's 45-day iMonnit Premiere trial, Standard Merchant Services' 30-day free trial on the 12-month plan, Sensor Easy's 30-day money-back guarantee), so a paid pilot has to include installation and a written HACCP log review to be worth paying for.

Inference: selling month-to-month with a 12-month discount (10-15%, mirroring Standard Merchant Services' declining per-sensor install fee and Sensitii's one-month-free annual billing) is a stronger SMB offer than multi-year annual contracts, because the loudest contract complaints in this category come from multi-year commitments (Jolt's 3-year annual quote) and non-cancellable terms (SmartSense's early-termination clause in a public school-district agreement requires paying the remaining fees through the end of the term).

Inference: do not lead with the cheapest hardware. ThermoWorks Cloud is free, Temp Stick is $149 once and TemperatureWise's Bluetooth sensor is $25 once, so a consultancy cannot win on device price; the paid work is installation, Wi-Fi/RF troubleshooting in walk-ins, alert routing that reaches someone at 2am, inspector-ready reports and replacing failed sensors - the exact items buyers complain are missing or unreliable in cheap options.

Inference: local presence is the pricing moat. SmartSense and ComplianceMate publish no prices and quote per asset count and term, and SmartSense's public agreement shows 12-month terms billed annually in advance; the only published NJ installed range ($1,200-$8,000) is a wide, undefined band. A Middlesex County provider that publishes a clear per-location price and shows up on site can charge in the upper half of that band without competing on sensor cost.
caveats: All prices retrieved 2026-11-12 from vendor pages unless a year is stated. Kitchen Brains figures come from a price list effective 1/1/2025, so they are roughly 22 months old.

TemperatureWise publishes a live price list on its own page and states the prices were checked 18 October 2026 against a 1 September 2026 price list; its hardware, gateway, cellular and door-contact prices are now published on that page and are reproduced here.

Several vendor pricing pages are script-rendered. ThermoWorks Cloud, ChirpDat, Monnit, Zip, Sensor Easy and Standard Merchant Services rendered prices on fetch. Monnit's $45.00 (6 sensors) and $120.00 (25 sensors) were confirmed on Monnit product pages; the $70/$175/$325 tiers come from the vendor's software page as indexed by search, not re-confirmed on a rendered product page.

ThermoWorks hardware prices (ThermaData WiFi loggers, walk-in kits) appear in search results for thermoworks.com but the product pages did not render prices on fetch, so no ThermoWorks hardware price is asserted here.

Sensitii's live pricing page is quote-only and shows no dollar figures, so no Sensitii price is included; an older $79-per-location/$7-per-sensor figure that appeared only in a search-indexed summary of that URL was dropped because the live page does not contain it.

Crafted Coolers/walkinboxesny.com, TempGenius, Elite Energy Management and Icedroid were reviewed during research but are not included as separate offerings to keep the set at twelve; none of their prices is asserted in this brief.
SmartSense, ComplianceMate and Testo Saveris publish no list prices; no Zest Labs or Squadle price is asserted because the figures seen came from search summaries of documents that were not opened.

Third-party figures (Jolt baseline and quotes, the ComplianceMate legacy tiers and annual estimate, the Missouri school-district bid, the Reddit DIY totals) are labeled by source type and are not vendor list prices.
The school-district bid table flattens on extraction, so only the two SmartSense-column figures quoted here ($175 per sensor with display, $400 per gateway) are treated as attributable.

No New Jersey restaurant invoice or signed quote was found, so the NJ-specific number here is a contractor's stated project range; the only other transaction-like figures are a Missouri school bid and contract terms, not local restaurant data.
data_gaps: No published price list was found for SmartSense by Digi, ComplianceMate or Testo Saveris US; all are quote-only in the pages opened, and the quote terms (asset counts, annual commitments, non-cancellable terms) matter more than the unit rate for a 5-200 staff buyer.
Zest Labs (Zest Fresh) publishes no price and prices by pallets managed, which does not map to a single deli or bakery; no usable figure found.
